question: Should Crabbox ship GitHub Codespaces as a built-in direct provider with the proposed aliases, local GitHub authentication, operator billing responsibility, and claim-bound destructive cleanup semantics?
rationale: Tests can establish implementation correctness, but they cannot choose whether Crabbox should permanently own this new built-in credential, billing, alias, and remote-deletion contract.

options.title: Accept after safe lifecycle proof
options.body: Ship the built-in provider after the claim/deletion and dirty-retention defects are repaired, the branch is rebased, and exact-head live proof succeeds.

options.title: Narrow the provider contract
options.body: Reduce aliases, configuration, or destructive behavior before accepting a smaller first-party surface.

options.title: Defer the built-in provider
options.body: Pause or close the PR if Crabbox should not own the Codespaces authentication, billing, and cleanup boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept after safe lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Ship the built-in provider after the claim/deletion and dirty-retention defects are repaired, the branch is rebased, and exact-head live proof succeeds.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the latest lifecycle-safety repairs and have the strongest current-main history on exact-claim destructive provider operations.
